newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Arab-Malaysian sees 30-40 pct/yr profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Arab-Malaysian sees 30-40 pct/yr profit growth.

text.p: Companies in the Arab-Malaysian group, one of Malaysia's biggest finance houses, are expected to maintain annual profit growth of 30-to-40 percent in the coming years, group chairman Azman Hashim said.

The firms, led by holding company Arab-Malaysian Corp Bhd (Amcorp), are expected to benefit from the country's more than eight percent a year economic growth rate, he told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
"I only measure our growth by the bottom line," Azman said. "Given the very strong economic growth environment, we expect to continue with the same pace (30-to-40 percent) of growth."
"We have come out with our half-yearly results. We expect the second half to be better than the first half," he said.
Amcorp net profit rose by 47.2 percent to 143.83 million ringgit ($57.08 million) in the six months to September 30.

AMMB Holdings, which encompasses the group's merchant bank, commercial bank and finance companies, reported a 49 percent rise in six-month net profit to 242.66 million ringgit. Arab-Malaysian Finance Bhd's first-half net profit was up 30 percent at 109.32 million ringgit.
Within the group, the banking and insurance companies will grow the fastest over the next few years, he said.
"All our units should be doing well, but our commercial bank, we expect to be the one with most prospects," he said.
He said after many years of not contributing to the group's bottom line, the insurance business would be boosted through a major internal thrust and strategic alliances.
To fund further expansion, Amcorp, the group holding company plans a capital raising exercise soon, Azman said.
Amcorp's issue was aimed at increasing shareholders' funds and followed similar fund-raising by other group companies.
"There will be soon an announcement to raise capital by Amcorp. That is the natural extension of the (group's fund-raising) exercise," he said. He declined to give details.
AMMB Holdings in September proposed two rights issues of stocks and bonds to raise up to 890 million ringgit to fund the growth of Arab-Malaysian Bank and the Arab-Malaysian Finance.
Analysts said the Amcorp issue would be big as it would have to subscribe to any planned rights portion in its 44.6 percent-owned AMMB Holdings Bhd and also fund its expansion.

The Arab-Malaysian Bank hopes to achieve tier-I status by 1998 under Malaysia's two-tier banking system by expanding its shareholders' funds to one billion ringgit in two years, from more than 500 million ringgit at present, Azman said.
He said group member Arab-Malaysian Finance had already qualified for tier-I status and had applied to Bank Negara, the central bank, for confirmation of its status.
Tier-I banks, merchant banks and finance companies are allowed to operate in a more liberal regulatory environment.
Azman said the fast-changing Malaysian financial sector had also necessitated a review of the group's structure.
"We will be looking into our group structure (to see) whether there is any better way of doing our business," he said. The aim is to "reorganise ourselves; it is an ongoing exercise".

"Lots of changes are going on with big banks coming in with big mergers. We are facing more big boys than before and they are not foreigners, they are locals. At the same time, along the horizon, we could be facing foreigners, too," he said.
($1=2.52 ringgit)
